# ADR-1143: A later version of a logged transcript replaces its session row

## Status

accepted. Narrows the replay skip of ADR-1084 for the session log: a row is skipped only when its transcript is the same bytes. ADR-1141 (delivery identity) and the profile dedup are unchanged.

## Context

Issue #716, acceptance item 3: modify an earlier turn and expose the replacement explicitly. The audit of slice 1 (`docs/audits/transcript-capture-producers-2026-11-05.md`, P1) found that the SessionEnd lifecycle keys a session-log row on the transcript stem (ADR-0497) and skipped any later row under that key (`_append_session`). A transcript that ended a second time, with turns appended or an earlier turn rewritten, kept its first row; the later version left no trace.

## Decision

1. A session-log row records `transcript`: the size in bytes and the SHA-256 of the transcript it was built from (`infrastructure/transcript_fingerprint.py`), or `null` when the event names no transcript or the file cannot be read.
2. A later SessionEnd under the same `sessionId` is compared with the logged fingerprint: the same SHA-256 is a `replay`; a longer file whose first logged bytes hash to the logged SHA-256 is `appended`; anything else is `rewritten`.
3. A replay keeps the logged row (ADR-1084's replay safety). An appended or rewritten version removes the logged row and appends the new one with `reconciliation`: `kind`, `replaced` (the logged fingerprint) and `replacedTimestamp`. The hook log names the replacement.
4. When either side has no fingerprint (a row written before this change, an unreadable file), nothing tells a replay from a new version: the logged row is kept, as before.

## Consequences

Positive: a grown or rewritten transcript reaches the session log once per version, and the row says which version it replaced and whether the earlier bytes were kept (`tests_py/hooks/test_session_log_reconciliation.py`).

Negative: the profile is still updated once per session and rollout file (ADR-1141): an appended or rewritten version replaces the log row but does not apply the profile update again, so the profile keeps the first version's figures. The Codex intake (`session_queue.py`) still keys a job on the session and the file, so a second SessionEnd of the same rollout after its receipt does not reach the lifecycle yet; that is the next slice of #716. Hashing reads the whole transcript once per SessionEnd, and once more up to the logged size when the hash differs. To go back, skip every row whose `sessionId` is logged, as before, and drop the `transcript` field.
